policies.policy_name: Role‑based permission to create Knowledge articles
policies.description: When a request to create a knowledge article is received, first call the **get_user** tool with the caller's `user_id` (extracted from the `x-itsm-user-token` or session). If the returned `role` field equals `admin`, `manager`, or `agent`, then invoke **create_knowledge_article** with the supplied payload. If the role is any other value (e.g., `reporter`), immediately stop processing and return a JSON‑formatted policy‑violation message indicating insufficient permissions.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.
Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables.
Reporter (reporter) | IT Service Consumption | Can view and update their own submitted Incidents/Requests. Can search Public Knowledge articles.

policies.policy_name: Mandatory fields for Knowledge article creation
policies.description: When invoking **create_knowledge_article**, the payload must contain a non‑empty **title** (string, max 120 characters) and a valid **owner_id** (user_id of an existing active user). Both fields are required by the API schema; omission or empty values must cause the request to be rejected before the tool is called.

policies.policy_name: Owner must be an active user
policies.description: When invoking the **create_knowledge_article** tool, check any `owner_id` supplied in the payload. Use the `get_user` (or `list_users` with `active=true`) tool to confirm that a user with that ID exists and that their `active` flag is true. If the user does not exist or is inactive, abort the creation request and return the error message "Owner must be an active user." This validation is required only for the `owner_id` field of the knowledge‑article creation operation.
references: User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.

archive.description: Only Knowledge articles whose **state** is set to **published** can be searched by users with the Reporter role.
references: Article Status: Only articles in knowledge.state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.
archive.comments:
The policy governs the *searchability* of knowledge articles for the Reporter role, not the creation of articles. The target tool is `create_new_knowledge_article`, which concerns inserting a new record. While the policy is about knowledge‑article objects, it does not impose any constraint on the fields that can be supplied to the creation endpoint, nor can it be validated prior to calling the tool (the state of the article is set after creation). Consequently the policy is not directly relevant or actionable for the creation tool, cannot be pre‑validated, and does not affect the tool's parameters. The policy description is clear and self‑contained, so no alternative description is needed. Score: 2 – the policy is clear but irrelevant to the specified tool.

archive.description: When creating or updating a Knowledge article, the **state** field must be one of the allowed enumeration values: **draft**, **review**, **published**, or **retired**.

It can be checked before invoking the tool, making it enforceable at runtime. While the rule also applies to the update operation, it is still relevant to the target creation tool, so it is not strictly tool‑specific. The allowed values are explicitly listed, so the policy is self‑contained. Overall the policy is clear, verifiable, and enforceable, meriting a score of 4 out of 5.
